author: vmadananth
title: GPU unit tests fail in a burst of 36 early-scheduled tests exiting with code 3 and no output on Windows runner
signature: gpu unit tests burst of early parallel test workers exit with code 3 and produce no test output or error before process exit|Infrastructure

failed_jobs.name: GPU unit tests
failed_jobs.symptom: 37 of 29276 ov_gpu_unit_tests failed: 36 exit immediately with exit code 3 and zero output within the first ~11s of the run (tests #4-#39), plus 1 unrelated known-flaky fp16 tolerance assertion (fusings_gpu/pooling_f32_scale.fp16_scale_out/1, tracked as pattern 7b64fedfacbfda60)

key_errors: FAILED TESTS (37/29276): ... 36 entries with no stack trace, only 'ov_gpu_unit_tests.exe <test name>' and elapsed time

src/plugins/intel_gpu/tests/unit/fusions/fusion_test_common.hpp(90): error: The difference between val_ref[i] and val_opt[i] is 3.0517578125e-05, which exceeds tolerance (fusings_gpu/pooling_f32_scale.fp16_scale_out/1)
root_cause: Identical recurrence of a previously-recorded pattern (f9292bee76d60b31, first seen on run 43457425018): in the first ~11 seconds of the 'Run GPU unit tests' step (gtest-parallel driving ov_gpu_unit_tests.exe), 36 of the earliest scheduled sub-process workers (test indices #4-#39, spanning unrelated suites: basic/convolution_random_smoke_test, convolution_grouped_fsv4_fsv16, fusings_gpu/conv_int8_scale_prelu_quantize_i8_eltwise_fp32_quantize_i8_vec) exit with code 3 and emit no gtest footer, assertion message, or stack trace -- only the standard 'Running main()'/'[ RUN ]' preamble before the process disappears. The remaining ~29,237 tests (including the same suites/fixtures re-run later) pass normally for the rest of the ~86-minute job. A 37th failure, fusings_gpu/pooling_f32_scale.fp16_scale_out/1, is the separately-tracked fp16 ULP tolerance flake (pattern 7b64fedfacbfda60), now seen 4 times. Because the exit-code-3 failures cluster entirely within the first few seconds of worker startup, span many unrelated test fixtures, and never recur later in the same run, this remains consistent with GPU/OpenCL driver or device-handle contention when gtest-parallel launches many ov_gpu_unit_tests.exe worker processes concurrently at start on this Windows self-hosted runner. This is unrelated to the merged PR #39011, which only touches intel_gpu FullyConnected weights-layout plumbing (infrastructure-only, no behavior change per its own description) and cannot explain a GPU-driver-level worker-startup race at test index #4.
reproduction_steps: Not reliably reproducible outside CI: it requires replicating the exact gtest-parallel worker concurrency and GPU/driver warm-up timing of the Windows self-hosted runner's integrated GPU at process startup. Locally, running `python gtest_parallel.py ov_gpu_unit_tests.exe` with a high worker count immediately after a cold driver/runner boot might reproduce a similar early-burst crash, but it is highly environment/timing dependent.
recommended_actions: Capture crashpad/minidump or stderr output from ov_gpu_unit_tests.exe worker processes that exit with non-gtest exit codes (gtest-parallel currently swallows this output); add stderr capture or verbose logging to retain the OpenCL/driver error that causes exit code 3.

Investigate whether gtest-parallel's default worker concurrency for ov_gpu_unit_tests.exe on this Windows runner should be reduced or staggered during startup to avoid simultaneous GPU/driver context acquisition races.
Check the runner image/driver version for known OpenCL driver cold-start contention issues when many processes request a device handle within the same few seconds.
Re-run the failed GPU unit tests job; given the burst-then-recovery pattern a plain retry is likely to pass.

Separately, consider raising the fp16 tolerance or marking fusings_gpu/pooling_f32_scale.fp16_scale_out/1 as known-flaky; it has now recurred 4 times (pattern 7b64fedfacbfda60) with an existing rerun-pattern proposal pending review.
prevention_strategies: Add stderr/crash capture for gtest-parallel worker processes so any future recurrence includes the actual OpenCL/driver error instead of a bare exit code, and consider a brief warm-up delay or reduced initial worker concurrency for the first wave of ov_gpu_unit_tests.exe processes on Windows GPU runners.
historical_context: This is the second recorded occurrence of pattern f9292bee76d60b31 (first seen 2026-11-14T04:18:42Z on run 43457425018, associated with unrelated PR #39824 touching only the GGUF frontend). The co-occurring fp16 tolerance flake (pattern 7b64fedfacbfda60) has now been seen 4 times across runs 43417057783, 43444472812, 43486543496 and this run, with an existing rerun-search-string proposal (`The difference between val_ref[i] and val_opt[i] is`) already pending human review.
